I feel that a revival of this page requires some showcasing that one can use these ideas to do something.

Agreed. I wonder if, to reduce clutter, some of the ideas can be migrated into a thread for "archived fragments" so the page is kept fresh with new ideas? Would take more effort to maintain, though…

That way, I feel that it could see more use as a source of inspiration (or challenge) for writers.

I feel like this is good so long as the ideas are solid. If it's just people tossing things in without much thought, those who use it as a resource may be discouraged if they have to slog through a bunch of ideas that aren't really good to start with.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Perhaps the Fragment page can be revamped into a hub wherein successful articles prompted by the fragments are linked to

Seconding this; SCP-1812 is based off of a blurb from this page from a loooooong while back, posted by Adam Henderson:

A second moon for earth. Small, just a captured asteroid. Can only be seen by someone if they are shown exactly what area of the sky it is in while being told there is a second moon there. People can be infected by something as minor as an already infected victim pointing at the right part of the sky and shouting about what an extra moon is doing there. Upon becoming able to see it, people will begin to be influenced by it, for example someone could see by light reflected off it, or drown in increased tides due to it.

For added creepiness, maybe a heavily expunged log of what happens when the foundation tries to land a robot probe on it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
To quote the Cracked article on the matter:

You may have noticed after your little impression of the Flash that your whole body's wreathed in fire. It's the friction of your body rubbing against a whole bunch of air molecules. The rest of us mortals aren't bothered by that because we move at the pace of a narcoleptic snail compared to you.

But, hey, maybe you've got some kind of fireproof suit. But Newton is still going to find a way to fuck you up. And if you thought friction was an asshole, wait until you hear what inertia is going to do to you. Let's say you hear about a totally awesome party across town and there's a girl there who wants your junk like, right this second. Zoom, off you go. But wait, what's that gooey shit on the ground behind you?

That, my friend, is your internal organs being liquefied from approximately 25 Gs and pushed out through your pores. Not that you'll care because the moment you do your immediate, Flash-like stop, your brain will go slamming into the front of your skull.

Read more: 7 Awesome Super Powers (Ruined by Science) | Cracked.com http://www.cracked.com/article_17185_7-awesome-super-powers-ruined-by-science.html#ixzz28djrp5U7

Soooooo….. Evidently, yes.

I like the idea of the excessively helpful humanoids. My advice for anyone tying to make them would be…

1. They are bad at doing stuff. They can't cook. They assume "rip the door off it's hinges" is the same as opening it. Shoelaces tied by them take hours to untangle.

2. They attack on assumed command. For example, if someone is mildly bothering the effected person cue said someone getting rushed by a hoard of crazy little vaguely humanoid creatures.
